answer: To stop hollow Sybil swarms, an agent registry can require zero-knowledge proofs over ePassports. Each operator proves possession of a state-signed credential and binds one agent key to a nullifier mixed with a beacon pulse, enforcing one active key per passport privately. Scaling fake agents forces attackers to acquire costly real documents per identity. Yet this defense sits on a narrow ledge, as rogue issuers can forge credentials and users lacking biometric passports are excluded.
